description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the perlvar INDEX walk (pv-err-vars), narrowed in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/backtick-ctx.pl (perl 5.40.3 vs main 093732ab):

    system("sh", "-c", "exit 3");  `true`;               print $?;          perl 0      PCL 768 (the system call's status, untouched)
    system("sh", "-c", "exit 3");  my $o = `true`;       print $?;          perl 0      PCL 768
    my $f = `sh -c "exit 2"`;                            print $? >> 8;     perl 2      PCL 3  (still the old one)

`system`, pipe `close` and `wait`/`waitpid` set `$?` correctly (battery pf-proc).  The run-and-check idiom above is how nearly every script that shells out detects failure; with no earlier `system` in the program `$?` simply stays 0, so a FAILING command looks like success.  Fix: the readpipe implementation (one function behind backticks, `qx`, `readpipe()`, the backtick heredoc -- #369 #702 #734 routed them together; check that they still share ONE path) stores the child's wait status into `$?` exactly as p-system does, in scalar AND list context, and -1 + `$!` when the shell cannot be started (#1920's rule).  Related, do not conflate: #1426 (an explicit `$? = N` does not stick), #2009 (`$?` in END).
Guard: rows beside #1920's.  Bar: `cl/` change => full sweep; companion op/exec.t + io/pipe.t.


=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
`p-backtick` now stores the child's raw wait status in `$?` in BOTH contexts,
through one helper reading SBCL's :EXITED / :SIGNALED, and a shell that cannot
be started gives perl's -1 with `$!` set (#1920's rule).  All four spellings
share the one path (#369/#702/#734 routed them together), verified by probe.

backtick-ctx.pl rows 1-7 identical to perl 5.40.3.  Guard: four rows in
Pl/t/system-block-01.t, inverse-verified on a 5ce155cb extraction.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 4 (0e6014eb).  p-backtick stores the child's raw wait
status in BOTH contexts through one helper that reads SBCL's :EXITED /
:SIGNALED; a shell that cannot start gives perl's -1 with $! set.  All four
spellings share the one path.  Normative statement: docs/ir-spec.md 8, the
`$?` row.  Guards: four rows in Pl/t/system-block-01.t.
CONSEQUENCE, measured: two sweep rows that were passing on a $? that was never
written now fail honestly -- recurse.t:129 (the child exhausts SBCL's binding
stack, #1929) and ref.t:530 (#2061).  Both entered
baselines/fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT with that cause; probe evidence in
scratch/s492c/logs/sweep-movers-probed-s495.txt.
SEQUEL: the handler-case this added around the whole body also swallowed a
perl die raised while the child ran -- fixed in member 11, task #2062.
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday): backticks / qx NEVER set `$?` -- ``my $out = `cmd`; die "failed" if $?;`` cannot see a failure (and reads a STALE status left by an earlier `system`)
